headline: Hiring a Contractor for Shower Removal: Mistakes to Avoid During Demolition
articleBody:
Tearing out an old shower looks simple with a sledgehammer, but hasty demolition frequently creates expensive damage to hidden plumbing, adjacent drywall, and structural studs. Knowing what can go wrong helps you preserve the rest of your bathroom while prepping for fresh finishes.

Here are the critical demolition mistakes to avoid:
1. Demolishing before verifying water shutoff. Never trust old fixture handles alone; always shut off the dedicated branch or main supply valves and test line pressure before removing shower valves.
2. Breaking adjacent drywall and floor tile outside the work zone. Failing to score clean boundary lines with an oscillating tool or utility knife causes torn sheetrock and cracked floor tiles that were never meant to be replaced.
3. Overlooking wet or rotted subflooring. Simply removing the surface pan without checking the condition of the subfloor underneath risks putting a new shower over decaying lumber.
4. Cutting or notching load-bearing framing. When removing wall panels, avoid cutting studs or structural framing to pry out plumbing runs.
5. Inadequate dust and debris containment. Shower demolition creates sharp tile fragments, mortar dust, and old fasteners; neglecting floor protection and plastic containment spreads fine dust throughout the home.

What to Do Next
